name: @agent-org/plugin-tailscale
description: The Tailscale exposure: the board's page and the worker terminal are served on the tailnet over HTTPS with `tailscale serve`, never on Funnel.

agentOrg.description: Serves the board and the worker terminal on the tailnet.

port.explanation: The loopback port the instance listens on.
port.breaks: A port another program holds stops the instance from starting, and the board cannot reach it.

edit.dangerous: A port another program holds stops the instance from starting, and the board cannot reach it.

uiPort.explanation: The loopback port the board's page listens on. It must differ from the instance's port.
uiPort.breaks: Equal to the instance's port it is refused by name; a taken port stops the page.

edit.dangerous: A port another program holds stops the page, and the board cannot be opened.

terminal.type: http or https address naming {workspace} or {pane}
terminal.explanation: Where a run's live terminal opens in a browser, with {workspace}, {pane} and {key} filled in per run. Absent means no terminal link. agent-org onboard writes it when the key is absent, and its terminal service serves it.
terminal.breaks: Any other shape is refused by name, and a grill run has no terminal to open.

tailnetPorts.type: object with ui and terminal ports
tailnetPorts.default: ui 9443, terminal 9444, read only with provider tailscale
tailnetPorts.explanation: The tailnet HTTPS ports the board and the terminal are served on, when the provider is tailscale.
tailnetPorts.breaks: Two equal ports, or one that is not a port, is refused by name.

edit.dangerous: The tailnet HTTPS ports the board and terminal are served on; a port another program holds stops them, and a wrong one serves them where no one looks.

tailnetPorts.ui.explanation: The tailnet HTTPS port the board is served on.
tailnetPorts.ui.breaks: Not a port is refused by name.

tailnetPorts.terminal.explanation: The tailnet HTTPS port the worker terminal is served on.
tailnetPorts.terminal.breaks: Not a port is refused by name.
